I am already thinking about this year the same way I always do: first keep the wheat-maize land steady, then leave some land in cotton for cash, and keep some garlic because it sells earlier and brings money home sooner. I am not a man who likes to gamble at 63. If I change too much and the weather turns bad, that loss is on my family. So I will mostly follow what has worked on my fields and what the better farmers in the village are doing, just a little careful on costs because some people in the house work outside and family labor is not always on hand.

For the 30 mu, I will keep 15 mu in wheat-maize rotation, 8 mu in cotton, and 7 mu in garlic. Wheat and maize are my base. Cotton gives cash if the price is decent, but it needs more watching and more picking. Garlic costs more for seed, but it brings in money earlier, so I still keep some. On wheat I will not save on fertilizer too much, because if wheat turns yellow in spring, yield drops fast and I cannot make that back later. Maize goes right after wheat harvest, so I will keep tillage simple and plant quickly. Cotton I will not push too hard with fertilizer because too much vegetative growth is also trouble. Garlic seed is expensive, so I keep the area limited to what I can manage well with family labor and some hired help when needed.
